speaker: provenzano
text: Thank you, Madam Clerk. I want to just say hi to the community at large and wish everybody a happy and healthy 2022. Certainly starting off in a challenging way. In that respect, I want to thank everybody in the community who has made sacrifices to work together to keep our community safe. I think it's become a bit difficult to follow all of the different advice that we've received over the last couple of weeks. I don't know if the advice has changed or evolved throughout the pandemic due to the different variants that we've had to contend with. For myself, for my own purposes, I've boiled it down to what I think are the core really important principles. I wanted to share that before we started our meeting. I think it's now very scientifically demonstrated that getting vaccinated is very helpful. It's helpful to you. It certainly reduces the chance that you will have a significant illness resulting from it. It's important to get vaccinated. If you have children and your children qualify for vaccines, it's important to consider getting your children vaccinated. I would encourage you to get your information from a trusted and reliable source as you make that decision. One of the things that we can all do is reduce our contacts, reduce the number of people that we are interacting with on a day-to-day basis as best we can. Stay home if you are not feeling well or if you have any symptoms and follow Algoma Public Health's guidance as it relates to isolating if you are a positive or if anybody in your house is a positive. Just as important, be patient and kind with one another as best as we can. This has been a very trying two years for all of us. Many different people are contending with many different things in their life and the pandemic is an extra, certainly significant stressor on top of that. Let's all dig deep and work hard to have patience for one another, help one another as and when we can and be kind to each other. Get vaccinated, get your children vaccinated, reduce your contacts as best as you can, stay home if you are not feeling well, and remember to, as best you can, be kind to each other. Before we start the meeting, Madam Clerk, I want to recognize that we are in the Huron-Robinson Treaty Territory, the land on which we are gathered, the traditional land of the Anishinaabe. It is the home of Garden River First Nation, Batchewana First Nation, the historic Sault Ste. Marie-Maidie Council. I want to also recognize that the head office of Mississippi Cree First Nation is here and the great work that the Urban Indigenous Friendship Centre does in our community. This territory is commonly and historically known as Bawating, and I appreciate it being shared with us. Madam Clerk, if we can start the meeting.

Whereas the foundation of Crime Stoppers remains the partnership between the community, law enforcement, and the media, Crime Stoppers work to educate the public and create awareness of illegal activities in an effort to promote safety, empowerment, and inclusion. Whereas this year's theme, Stop the Crime of Human Trafficking, is more than a call to action. It represents an opportunity to increase awareness of this devastating crime that targets people from all backgrounds. Crime Stoppers accepts tips on sex and labor trafficking and wants people to be aware they can safely and honestly report crime through their toll-free line and web tip option. text: Okay. Okay. Well, thank you very much. So just as a reminder, future Sault Ste. Marie is about implementing the community's collective vision to build a city where people want to visit, live, and do business. The future Sault Ste. Marie plan was developed through extensive community consultation from 2016 to 2017, with over 4,800 people being involved, including youth. Following the conclusion of the plan, both the city and Fednor committed funds towards the implementation, and a team was hired in 2018. The project continues to date, with Fednor graciously providing an extension to December 2023 to account for the complications that arose from COVID. In terms of implementing the plan, we know through best practices that the only way to achieve resilience in the community is to look at a four-pillar approach. And in doing so, through future Sault Ste. Marie, we've identified the pillar of cultural vitality, economic growth and diversity, environmental sustainability, and social equity. Through those four pillars, we've identified eight overarching goals that we aim to achieve throughout the project. To date, we have a number of exciting projects that have been completed, and others that are currently in progress. By establishing a framework for future... Sorry, by establishing a framework for community development and setting clear priorities, future Sault Ste. Marie has been able to advance beneficial projects that cross over multiple pillars and overarching goals. Moving forward, the framework and goals of future Sault Ste. Marie will guide our community development strategy. Community development roundtable will continue to be engaged and provide input on some of the initiatives on a go-forward basis. And as we move forward with our community development, economic and tourism strategies, we will ensure that they are fully integrated with the principles of future Sault Ste. Marie. In order to assist us with implementing these plans, we have transitioned a number of the future SSM project roles into permanent full-time positions within the municipality. As a quick overview of some of the high-level community outcomes that we've had to date by pillar, I'll just run through this following list. In terms of cultural vitality, we've established the new Cultural Vitality Committee and increased the funding for local arts organizations from 53,000 up to 144,000. And we've established numerous collaborations with various partners around the community. In terms of economic growth and diversity, despite the pandemic, we've had major growth projects announced, including projects from Algoma Steel, the PUC, and Tenaris. With respect to environmental sustainability, Council endorsed the Community GHG Reduction Plan and also retained a full-time dedicated position for environmental sustainability and established an Environmental Sustainability Committee. With respect to social equity, we've recently concluded the Community Safety and Well-Being Plan. We've installed the Pride Crosswalk, and we've established a social equity program that is included as part of the Community Development Fund. As we move on towards our eight overarching goals, we have launched numerous promotional campaigns for the purpose of attracting new residents and businesses to the community, all under the banner of our new brand. And we most recently received funding to assist with the attraction of healthcare professionals to the city. As we move to refocus our economic and community development, we have integrated and migrated all economic development and tourism staff into the city and ensured that their work now aligns with the goals and principles of future Sault Ste. Marie. As we move to build our labour force, staff have worked directly with local industry and partners to find skilled labour to meet their needs, and we've also engaged in the development of the R3 strategy, which we intend to move forward. We've also hosted external job fairs and provided support for employers on an ongoing basis. As we move to invite immigration and welcome newcomers, we've established the RNIP program and continue to advance it making over 120 positive recommendations for the community. We've also integrated the reporting structure of the local immigration partnership within the community development department and have received most recently funding from FedNord to assist with the implementation of the RNIP program. Moving on to the goals, you know, I'd like to claim success for the growth of post-secondary institutions, but in perfect honesty, both Sioux College and Algoma U have been doing a phenomenal job on their own. We have provided assistance with some marketing and also dedicated community development funds to Algoma U and Sioux College to support the City Studio project as well as an engineering program at Sioux College. We continue to advance our Indigenous relationships through the Bawading Advisory Circle and have engaged with our Indigenous partners on numerous projects throughout the duration of future Sioux St. Marie. We work to improve our community well-being through the expansion of our mountain bike trail networks, the installation of kayak docks along the St. Mary's River and bus services now to Pointe du Chien. There's ongoing work occurring related to the revitalization of the downtown with the redevelopment of Bay Street, the construction of the downtown plaza, the streetscape designed for Queen Street and Spring and the establishment of downtown safety pilot program. In terms of some high-level data points, future Sioux St. Marie has led the attraction of Rolling Picture Company to the City and that has resulted in approximately a $1 million investment in the community to date. And I had identified six staff hired locally but just on Friday found out that they've hired a couple more, so great news. And they're also continuing to look at what other opportunities they can bring to the community. In addition to this, future Sioux St. Marie staff have secured over $1.6 million in federal and provincial grants for the City and community, including $425,000 in grants for local social services and Indigenous organizations, approximately $135,000 in grants for environmental initiatives, just over $1 million in grants to support economic development and tourism and $75,000 to assist with the recruitment of medical professionals. In addition to this, staff have completed the following community plans, including the Cultural Plan, the Greenhouse Gas Emissions Plan, the Community Safety and Wellbeing Plan, the Mountain Bike Trail Master Plan, a feasibility study specific to the Kinsman Centre and are also in the process, as mentioned previously, of implementing the ARNET plan with over 120 candidates recommended and direct support to companies in terms of the recruitment and placement of skilled labour. So with that, I'll stop my presentation. I know that there's a far more extensive one included with the Council report.
